disposition_reason: A host in standby cannot accept an OS SSH command, so the source's preceding BMC-UART step must be treated as evidence that `powerctrl.sh` belongs to an always-on management domain unless engineering says otherwise. Power-on success also has phases: GPIO assertion, rail-good, POST and OS readiness. Combining `power_on; sleep 5; power_status; uptime` in one host session skips the domain transition and substitutes a fixed delay for staged oracles. The valid contract uses a secure controller session for the single action and independent observation, followed by a new host session only after boot. test_case.test_name: Power On (GPIO) — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify that the platform GPIO power controller can transition a host from the defined standby state to on and that the host completes a normal boot with expected system health.
required_package: SUT/BMC identity and authoritative always-on location, version/hash/owner of `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh`
Exact `power_on` GPIO/rail target, pulse/level behavior, idempotence and expected command response
Authoritative standby definition including AC, standby rails, host/chassis state and no-active-workload evidence
Secure BMC/controller access and independent UART/rail/chassis power observer
Power-on, rail-good, POST and OS-network/service timeout sequence with abort criteria
Owner-approved recovery path and post-boot firmware/device/filesystem/service/log health oracle
test_case.test_command: Identify the exact always-on controller, script version and `power_on` semantics; confirm AC present, standby rails stable and host actually off without active workloads; obtain approval for one transition; from secure BMC/UART/controller access invoke the literal source command once; independently timestamp rail/chassis power and boot-stage changes; after OS network readiness, open a separate verified host session to collect uptime and complete health/log checks; stop without automatic retry on any ambiguous state or boot failure.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test. Criteria: Command should send successfully. System will power on. "

safety_gate: Do not invoke `power_on` until target identity and stable standby/off state are independently confirmed
Run the transition from the documented always-on controller, not through an impossible host-OS SSH session
Use secure injected credentials and verified controller/host identity; reject `sshpass -p` and disabled host-key checking
Capture one command and independent rail/chassis/UART transition timeline with bounded timeouts
Stop if already on, standby is inconsistent, power rails sequence incorrectly, POST stalls, devices disappear or critical logs appear
Do not issue another power-on, power-cycle or reset automatically; use the separately approved recovery path
expected_evidence: SUT/BMC/controller identity, script path/version/hash/owner and exact GPIO/power-on semantics
Pre-action AC/standby-rail/chassis-off state, idle/no-workload proof and approval timestamp
Secure controller session and exact `power_on` stdout/stderr/exit/timestamp
Independent rail/chassis/BMC/UART transition timeline through POST and OS readiness with timeouts
Separate secure host session showing boot ID/uptime, expected devices/services/filesystems and power status
BMC SEL plus OS boot/kernel/service logs, recovery actions if any and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The project must provide the always-on controller transport. A host SSH wrapper may be used only for post-boot health, never as an implicit substitute for the controller-side source command.

source_conflict.reason: The source consistently describes one standby-to-on GPIO transition followed by normal operation. The exact script domain and standby oracle are underspecified project inputs; the infeasible SSH wrapper belongs to historical reviews, not the Master source.
